chunks: Hadith 5127 — Muḥammad ibn ʿAbdillāh ibn Hilāl narrated from his father, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
I said to him: “Inform me about the thief: why is his right hand and his left foot cut off, and not his right hand and his right foot?”

He said: “How excellent is what you have asked. If his right hand and his right foot were cut off, he would fall onto his left side and would not be able to stand. But if his right hand and his left foot are cut off, he remains balanced and stands upright.”

He said: I said, “May I be your ransom, how can he stand when his foot has been cut off?” He said: “The cutting is not from where you think it is cut. Rather, the foot is cut from the ankle, and part of his foot is left for him upon which he may stand, perform salat (prayer), and worship Allah, Mighty and Majestic.”

I said: “Then from where is the hand cut?” He said: “The four fingers are cut off, and the thumb is left for him, so that he may rely upon it in salat (prayer) and wash his face with it for salat (prayer).”

key_terms.تُقْطَعُ: is cut off; refers to the prescribed legal amputation
key_terms.ٱلسَّارِقِ: the thief who is subject to the legal punishment discussed here
key_terms.ٱلصَّلَاةِ: salat (prayer), whose performance is considered in the application of the ruling
key_terms.ٱلْإِبْهَامُ: the thumb, which is left intact
key_terms.ٱلْكَعْبِ: the ankle, the point from which the foot is cut
key_terms.ٱلْيُسْرَىٰ: the left side, specifically the left foot in this ruling
key_terms.ٱلْيُمْنَىٰ: the right side, specifically the right hand or right foot in this hadith

ai.seo_question: Why are the right hand and left foot of a thief cut off in Islamic law rather than the right hand and right foot?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the legal reasoning behind cutting the thief’s right hand and left foot rather than both right limbs. The Imam عليه السلام clarifies that the prescribed punishment preserves the person’s ability to stand, perform salat (prayer), and continue worship, and he also specifies the exact portions of the foot and hand that are cut.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.5127 - Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Hilal narrated from his father from Abu Abdullah (as) who said:
I asked Imam (as): "Tell me why the right hand and the left foot of a thief are cut off, but not the right hand and the right foot?"

Imam (as) replied: "What a good question you have asked! If his right hand and right foot were cut off, he would fall onto his left side and would not be able to stand. But when his right hand and left foot are cut off, he remains balanced and can stand upright."

I said: "May I be your ransom, how can he stand when his foot has been cut off?"
Imam (as) replied: "The cutting is not as you perceive it. The foot is cut off from the ankle, leaving part of the foot so that he can stand on it, perform prayer, and worship Allah (swt), the Mighty and Majestic."

I asked: "From where is the hand cut off?"
Imam (as) replied: "The four fingers are cut off, and the thumb is left for him so that he may lean on it during prayer and wash his face for prayer."
